_comment: Nightly mutation testing over the pure engine (packages/core). A green unit suite that survives every mutant is not a suite: it pins behaviour nobody asserted. The recorded score and the threshold are in docs/P1-REPORT.md — 'the mutation job is green' is not a measurement. The P1 gate clause 'Stryker score >= threshold nightly' is NOT met yet and the report says so: only `packages/core/src/day/` has ever been scored (71.28%, 968 mutants, 12 min 19 s), the whole engine is 9,802 mutants, and Stryker refuses a tree whose initial test run is red — which the merged P1 tree still is. Until a whole-engine number exists the nightly REPORTS (continue-on-error in the workflow) and `thresholds.break` is a documented derivation, not a gate anyone has validated.
mutate_comment: Every engine module under packages/core/src, and nothing else. The three exclusions are deliberate: *.test.ts is the suite doing the killing; index.ts is a barrel of re-exports whose mutants are all equivalent; journey/** is the phase gate's own harness (it scans the repo and drives a 30-day trace — it is test infrastructure that happens to live in a .ts file, and mutating it measures the gate, not the engine).
mutator_comment: The Regex mutator is off, and the reason is measured, not stylistic. weapon-regex negates predefined classes (\d -> \D, \s -> \S) and applies the same rule to \v, producing \V — which is an INVALID ESCAPE under the `u` flag. packages/core/src/security/sanitise.ts carries /[\t\n\r\f\v]+/gu, and because every mutant is instrumented inline, rollup fails to parse the whole file: measured 2026-09-11 on the merged P1 engine, the initial dry run died with `SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: /[\t\n\r\f\V]+/gu: Invalid escape` and Stryker produced no score at all. One mutator off with a written reason beats no measurement; the loss is regex mutants only, and docs/P1-REPORT.md records it as an open item.
thresholds_comment: high/low colour the report. `break` is the number Stryker exits non-zero below. IT IS DERIVED FROM ONE MODULE, NOT FROM THE ENGINE: 70 comes from `packages/core/src/day/` alone, measured at 71.28% over 968 mutants on 2026-09-11 (docs/P1-REPORT.md §Mutation, with the per-file table — rollover.ts 61.85%, config.ts and state.ts 44.44%). 1.3 points of headroom on 10% of the engine is not evidence about the other 8,834 mutants, so .github/workflows/mutation.yml keeps `continue-on-error: true` and the nightly REPORTS the score rather than gating on it. The first whole-engine run replaces this number with a measured one, at which point continue-on-error comes off in the same commit. Raised, never lowered, afterwards.
timeout_comment: A mutant that loops forever must be reported as a timeout rather than hanging the job. The engine's slowest unit tests are the four-zone properties at 10,000 cases per zone (~3.5 s locally, ~2.5x that on ubuntu-latest), so the factor is generous on purpose: a timeout counted as 'killed' is free score.
dryRunTimeoutMinutes_comment: Stryker's default is 5 minutes and the P1 engine blows straight through it. The suite is 27 s on its own, but the dry run collects PER-TEST coverage over 1,125 tests, 222 of which are fast-check properties at 10,000 cases (the four-zone ones at 40,000). Measured 2026-09-11 on the merged P1 engine: the dry run was still going at 5:03 and Stryker aborted with `Initial test run timed out!` and no score. 30 minutes is the headroom that buys, and it is the DRY RUN only — a mutant that hangs is still caught by timeoutMS.
incremental_comment: Nightly, over 9,802 mutants, a cold run is hours. Incremental mode re-tests only the mutants whose file or covering tests changed since the last report, and .github/workflows/mutation.yml caches that report between runs. The first run after a cache miss is still a cold run, which is why the job's timeout is generous.
